Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with clinical presentation of acute continuous vertigo with nausea and ear buzzing without hearing loss or focal neurological deficits  
- Differential diagnosis:  
  • Labyrinthitis (vestibular neuritis) – High likelihood; fits classic presentation of continuous vertigo, nausea, and ear buzzing despite absence of a recent viral illness and ear pain  
  • Posterior circulation transient ischemic attack (TIA)/stroke – Moderate likelihood; acute dizziness and imbalance present, but no neurological deficits documented  
  • Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) – Low to moderate likelihood; prior brief vertigo episode supports, but current continuous symptoms without positional triggers lessen likelihood  
  • Acoustic neuroma and hypoglycemia considered less likely based on symptom acuity and absence of progressive hearing loss or diabetic history  
- Conflict noted: None; DDx aligns with transcript information  

Management Plan  
- Initiate symptomatic treatment with prescribed medication (name not specified) one tablet three times daily for 10 days to address middle ear inflammation and symptoms  
- Schedule in-person ear examination and neurological assessment including blood pressure and gait evaluation with physician  
- Advise urgent emergency department presentation if new neurological symptoms occur (weakness, severe headache, vomiting) or worsening condition  
- Provide reassurance and instructions regarding medication intake (may take without food if nauseated)  
- Confirm pharmacy for prescription collection (Lloyd pharmacy)
